Subject: Invoice line-item discrepancy: sample proration

Hi Grace / Vanessa,

We just received the August invoice (attached: ACME_sample_invoice_20280831.pdf) and noticed a recurring line item that looks like a proration/rounding mismatch. For one of our burst jobs the invoice shows a minimum charge of 1 unit where our expectation — based on the proration rules discussed during contracting — was that those short-lived calls would be aggregated and prorated to 0.4 units.

I attached the invoice and a short csv with the call samples (proration-sample-calcs.csv). Can you confirm:
- Which billing quantum applied to these calls?
- Whether prefix reuse / KV caching was considered in the proration?
- If any one-off minimums were triggered by a packaging rule we missed?

This is blocking our internal reconciliation. If needed, we can hop on a 20-min call this week.

Thanks,
Alyssa

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the heads up and for sending the samples.

Quick summary from our side: based on the data you sent it looks like two short calls in the sample window did trigger the per-call minimum (our current packaging floor for your pilot sku is 1 unit per independent call when the call duration or token count falls below the configured microfloor). That said, I agree this looks like a proration edge with burst aggregation — the csv you attached is exactly the sort of input we need to reconcile.

Action items from Redwood:
- Vanessa will validate how prefix/KV cache reuse influenced those calls.
- Ben (copying) will run the proration math and propose a one-time adjustment if the invoice applied rounding incorrectly.
- I can schedule a short call if you'd like walk-throughs and to confirm the updated invoice.

Proposed call slots: Thu 9/7 10:00 AM PT or Thu 9/7 2:00 PM PT — let me know which works.

Apologies for the noise — we'll sort this out quickly.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Sep 2028 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Invoice line-item discrepancy: sample proration

Grace / Vanessa — digging in and attaching a quick calc (internal) that walks through the two sample calls Alyssa sent. Key points:

1) Billing quantum applied: per our deployed SKU for ACME-ENTERPRISE-2028 the billing quantum is 1 unit per call floor for microbursts unless there is a contiguous prefix match that reduces the effective per-call metering. In the sample, call A and call B are 18s apart and landed on different routing windows, so they were not auto-aggregated by our current batching window (5s continuity threshold).

2) KV/prefix reuse: Vanessa confirmed (see her note below) there was partial KV reuse on call B but not enough to meet our 90% affinity threshold for aggregation into the prior call. That explains why call B hit the floor independently.

3) Rounding/proration: The proration calculation applied was standard: sum(tokens)/quantum rounded to nearest integer after applying microfloor. Because each call individually fell under the microfloor, you saw two 1-unit charges instead of a single 0.4 + 0.4 aggregated expectation.

Proposed remediation (we recommend):
- Apply a one-time credit equal to the difference between billed minimums and the theoretical aggregated proration for the sample window (credit = 1.2 units @ your effective per-unit rate).
- Adjust the batching continuity threshold for your tenant from 5s to 30s for burst workloads to prevent near-term reoccurrence (requires ops change to routing policy; flagged to infra).
- We'll include a short note on the updated invoice line explaining the credit and the configuration change.

If that's acceptable I can draft the credit memo and Vanessa can confirm the ops timeline.

Ben

Next steps for us: please send an updated invoice with the credit and a short config note we can attach to our GL. Also send the DocuSign link for the minor amendment to confirm the batching window change to 30s (we'll need that signed for our change control).

Call: Thu 9/7 10:00 AM PT works for our team.
